topic: CCB in shared custody: if the child lives with you 40% to 60% of the time (the other parent the rest, at a different address), each parent receives 50% of the payment they would get with the child 100% of the time, calculated on each parent's own adjusted family net income; over 60% = full custody, only that parent eligible; under 40% = not eligible, should not apply

example.note: example (not a CRA rule): Jordan and Casey separated; their 5-year-old alternates weeks (7 of 14 nights = 50%). July 2026–June 2027 maximum for a child under 6 is $8,157/yr; in shared custody each parent gets half of their own full-custody amount, so at most $4,078.50 each (only at low adjusted family net income); the actual halves differ with each parent's income.

sources.shared: canada.ca CRA 'Who can apply – Canada child benefit': shared custody if the child lives with you 40% to 60% of the time; each individual gets 50% of the payment they would have received if the child lived with them 100% of the time; payments calculated on each parent's own adjusted family net income; more than 60% = full custody; less than 40% = not an eligible individual (via canada.ca search excerpts 2026-11-05)
